newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes touch lower, PGMs weaken.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes touch lower, PGMs weaken.

text.p: Precious metals prices were barely changed in afternoon trading on Wednesday after the platinum group metals (PGMs) weakened overnight, dealers said.
"The PGMs have softened slightly and for gold we could be around this level for some time to come," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $341.60 per ounce after $342.05 this morning and $342.15 on Wednesday afternoon.
The August Comex gold contract was unchanged at $343.70 having edged higher briefly on the opening.
Dealers said business was very light and the bias was towards a drift lower as the summer lull set in.
However there was little risk of a serious raid on the downside to take a profit on selling short.
"Support might lessen from around the $340,00 but I don't see much incentive for people to make a big play on the downside," one dealer said.

Some support was coming from a weaker dollar in Europe but there was little impact in the foreign exchanges from the unrevised April U.S. durable goods orders and first quarter unit labour costs being revised lower.

Silver returned to levels around $4.72/$4.74 before a brief buying move by the funds on New York Comex futures raised prices about six cents. There was no follow through in the Far East or Europe and the move was reversed shortly after the Comex opening, dealers said.
Liquidity continued to improve in the PGMs and swap rates eased slightly as the markets edged towards normal from the ultra tight conditions of a couple of weeks ago.
"There is no new information from Moscow or Japan so we are assuming that Russia will start delivering within a few weeks," one dealer said.
Russia the leading exporter of palladium and second biggest supplier of platinum has not shipped either metal since last December due to domestic political wrangling.
Prices of both metals came off sharply on the Japanese Tocom futures market when a weaker yen encouraged selling which in turn sent dollar-denominated spot prices lower.
Platinum was indicated at $406.00/$411.00 down from a $417.00/$421.00 close and palladium was $6.00 lower at $189.00/$194.00.
